The '''2000–01 Football League Cup''' (known as the '''[[Worthington Brewery|Worthington]] Cup''' for sponsorship reasons) was the 41st staging of the [[EFL Cup|Football League Cup]], a knockout competition for England's top 92 [[association football|football]] clubs.

The competition began on 22 August 2000, and ended with the final on 25 February 2001 at the [[Millennium Stadium]] in [[Cardiff]] as [[Wembley Stadium (1923)|Wembley Stadium]] had been closed for a rebuild.

The tournament was won by [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]], who beat [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]] 5–4 on penalties after a 1–1 draw after extra-time. [[Robbie Fowler]] put Liverpool in front after half an hour but a [[Darren Purse]] penalty salvaged the game for Birmingham in the final minute of normal time.

This edition was the last with two-legged ties in the first two rounds.

==First round==
The 70 [[Football League First Division|First]], [[Football League Second Division|Second]] and [[Football League Third Division|Third Division]] clubs compete from the first round. Each section is divided equally into a pot of seeded clubs and a pot of unseeded clubs. Clubs' rankings depend upon their finishing position in the [[1999-2000 in English football|1999–2000 season]]. Therefore, the 20th place from the Premier League in 2000, [[Watford F.C.|Watford]] was the top seed, and the club newly promoted to the Third Division, [[Kidderminster Harriers F.C.|Kidderminster Harriers]], were bottom seeds. The first legs took place on 22 and 23 August and the second legs on 5 and 6 September.

==Second round==
The 35 winners from the first round joined the [[Premier League]] clubs not participating in European competition along with [[Wimbledon F.C.|Wimbledon]] and [[Sheffield Wednesday F.C.|Sheffield Wednesday]], the top two relegated teams from Premier League the last season. The ties were played over two legs, with the first legs from 19 to 20 September and the second legs on 26 and 27 September. Two second leg matches were played on 2 October.

==Semi-finals==

''Birmingham City win 4–2 on aggregate''

==Final==
{{further|2001 Football League Cup Final}}
The 2001 Worthington Cup Final was played on 25 February 2001 and was contested between [[Football League First Division|First Division]] side [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]] and Premier League team [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] at the [[Millennium Stadium]], [[Cardiff]]. Liverpool won the game 5–4 on penalties following a 1–1 draw after extra time.
